title: Outage notice framing and Terraform handoff for private sites
body:
Purpose
This note shapes customer-facing communications and the Terraform-centric operational handoff for Planned Maintenance / Upgrade windows for private deployments (VPC or on-prem). It pairs clear SLA/SLO framing with a concrete, copy-ready set of templates and a concise Terraform preflight and upgrade checklist meant for solutions engineers and SREs.

Audience
- Customer success and account owners preparing tenant notifications
- Solutions engineers running hands-on upgrades
- SREs and release leads owning rollback and verification

Principles (short)
- Clarity over jargon: customers want to know impact, duration, actions required.
- Single source of truth: status page message is canonical; emails and portal messages should point there.
- Minimal surprise: escalate from informative to urgent only if scope or ETA changes.
- Terraform-first ops: treat IaC as source of truth for topology and post-upgrade assertions.

Send cadence (recommended)
- T-72h: Informational — planned window, expected duration, affected services, link to preflight checklist and support contact.
- T-24h: Reminder — short subject, reminder of impact, expected read-only period if any.
- T-2h: Final alert — start time, brief runbook link, how we’ll notify completion.
- T+1h: Early completion notice if finished early.
- T+24h: Postmortem + verification checklist and guidance to open any regressions.

Templates (copy/paste-ready)
1) Scheduled maintenance — email / portal subject
Subject: Scheduled maintenance — Redwood Inference private deployment (windows: {start_iso} — {end_iso} UTC)

Email body (scheduled)
Hello {customer_name},

We will perform a scheduled maintenance for your Redwood private deployment on {start_local} (UTC {start_iso}) with an estimated completion by {end_local} (UTC {end_iso}). The maintenance will include: kernel patch, inference runtime upgrade to {target_version}, and Terraform reprovisioning of the load-balancer resources.

Expected impact: {brief_impact_line — e.g., brief degraded write latency, short restarts of inference workers}.

What you need to do: No action required for most customers. If you have pinned model versions or custom integrations, please confirm that your integration will tolerate brief reconnects.

Canonical status page: {status_page_url}
Support contact during window: {oncall_contact}, escalation: {escalation_email}

We will post a completion note on the status page and follow up with a verification checklist at T+24h.

Regards,
Redwood Private Operations

2) Urgent outage — short subject
Subject: Urgent: service disruption for your Redwood private deployment

Body (urgent)
Hello {customer_name},

We are investigating an unexpected disruption affecting inference traffic for your private deployment. Engineers are actively diagnosing. Current symptoms: {symptom_bullets}.

What we are doing: {one-line-action-items}. Estimated next update: {eta_minutes} minutes.

If your team needs to trigger a failover to hosted API or fallback model, please open the linked runbook: {runbook_link} or contact {oncall_pager}.

We’ll provide continuous updates until resolved.

3) Rollback completed — subject
Subject: Rollback complete — private deployment restored to {previous_version}

Body
Hello {customer_name},

We have completed a rollback to {previous_version} at {completion_iso} and restored normal traffic flow. The service is now operational and we’re running post-rollback validation checks.

If you see anomalies, please reply to this thread or open an incident at {incident_link}.

Status page snippets (short)
- Maintenance planned: "Planned maintenance affecting inference worker restarts for private deployment {site_name}. Expected window: {start_iso} — {end_iso}. No action required unless otherwise notified."
- In progress: "Maintenance in progress for {site_name}: rolling restart. Some requests may see short 5xx spikes; retry is recommended."
- Complete: "Maintenance complete. Please validate model responses and surface any regressions to {support_email}."

SMS / Pager short forms
- T-2h: "Redwood maintenance for {site_name} starts in 2h. Check {status_page_url}."
- Urgent: "Redwood outage — {site_name} impacted. Updates: {status_page_url}."

Tone and escalation guidance
- Keep copy factual and vendor-neutral (avoid apologetic legal language)
- For SLA-impacting windows (where SLO risk > 50%), include explicit credit/compensation contact line and mark message as "SLA-impacting" in the subject.

Customer-facing Impact Table (plain text)
- Affected components: inference runtime, KV cache, control-plane agent (if applicable)
- Expected degradation: transient 5xx or 504 for < 2 minutes per worker restart, or a short read-only mode for metadata endpoints
- Estimated worst-case outage per affected tenant: {worst_case_minutes}
- SLA consequence: may count toward availability SLO if not mitigated by fallback policies

Terraform-centric preflight and handoff notes (concise)
Overview: treat Terraform as the authoritative representation of desired infra. Before communicating to customers, complete the preflight below and attach the state snapshot to the internal ticket.

Preflight checklist (run this BEFORE T-72h communication is finalized)
- terraform workspace select {tenant_workspace} && terraform plan -var-file={tenant_vars}
- Take a state snapshot: terraform state pull > state-{tenant}-{yyyyMMdd}.json and upload to secure ticket
- Confirm provider plugin versions match the runbook matrix (aws, gcp, onprem-provider v{min_supported})
- Verify that any KMS/HSM rotation steps have a test vector and customer key permissions are valid
- Validate that autoscaling policies and health-check endpoints are unchanged by the plan
- Confirm that network ACL changes are staged as separate PRs (no mixing infra+runtime code in a single deploy)

Upgrade steps (engineer checklist)
- Step 0: Branch & PR: branch: upgrades/{tenant}/{target_version}; open PR referencing Jira {jira_key} and include plan output
- Step 1: Snapshot backups: database, disk images, and terraform state snapshot as above
- Step 2: Canary: apply to 1 non-critical node or tenant replica using terraform apply -target=module.node[0] and run smoke tests (see post-upgrade-verification)
- Step 3: Sequential rollout: apply in batches, monitor CPU, memory, latency, error-rate (SLO dashboards), and KV hit-rate
- Step 4: Post-apply validation: run the validation script (./tools/validate-deployment.sh --tenant {tenant})
- Step 5: Finalize: tag terraform state and merge PR when all canaries pass

Terraform quicknotes (common pitfalls & fixes)
- State drift: if terraform plan shows surprise diffs from the running control plane, run an immediate terraform refresh and annotate the ticket with drift details.
- Secret rotation: avoid embedding new secrets in the same apply as infra changes; stage them first to prevent transient auth failures.
- Provider mismatches: when provider upgrades are required, run a provider-only plan first and coordinate across tenants to avoid simultaneous rolling restarts.

Post-upgrade verification (smoke tests)
- endpoints: /health, /metrics, /v1/generate (short prompt), /v1/kv/status
- acceptance criteria: 200 for /health, metrics show < 10% increase in p95 latency, no new 5xx errors in last 10 minutes
- sample validation commands: curl -sS {tenant_endpoint}/health | jq .status; ./perf/run_short_request.sh {tenant_endpoint}

Rollback guidance (fast path)
- If canary shows fatal regressions, trigger terraform rollback: git revert <upgrade-commit> && terraform apply --auto-approve -var-file={tenant_vars} OR apply a saved state snapshot (state replace + force) as last resort.

Escalation matrix (communications)
- Level 1 (info): Account owner + CS rep (email + portal post)
- Level 2 (affecting SLO): Operations lead + Solutions Eng + CS manager (email + urgent status page update)
- Level 3 (SLA breach / multi-tenant outage): Exec on-call + Legal + Customer success director (direct call + formal incident report)

Internal handoff checklist to attach to ticket (must be completed before merge)
- state snapshot uploaded
- terraform plan file attached
- smoke-test results from canary node
- contact oncall and scheduled pager rotation set
- communications drafts attached for T-72h/T-24h/T-2h

Suggested Subject Line Variations (for AB test)
- "Planned runtime upgrade — {site_name}: brief restarts expected"
- "Maintenance window notice for {site_name} — {start_local}"
- "Action required? No — maintenance for {site_name} scheduled {start_local}"

Example timeline (text)
- 03:00 UTC: Begin canary node apply (1 node)
- 03:10 UTC: Run smoke tests on canary; monitor metrics for 15m
- 03:25 UTC: Begin batch apply (10% nodes)
- 04:30 UTC: Finish rollout, start verification script
- 05:00 UTC: Completion notice and status page update

Short FAQ to include in portal post
Q: Will my models be impacted?
A: Models will keep their data and versions. There may be brief reconnects; responses should be retried.

Q: Is this maintenance covered by my SLA?
A: Planned maintenance windows are generally excluded from availability calculations; if this maintenance becomes a service outage beyond the planned window, we will treat it as a potential SLO impact and follow the incident and credit process.

Q: Can you avoid restarts?
A: Not for runtime or kernel patching — restarts ensure consistent state and security posture. We aim to minimize impact with rolling restarts.

Notes and follow-ups
- Attach this doc as the canonical comms bundle for the ticket and keep a thread for the final postmortem.
- If customers run special networking (air-gapped / private peering), coordinate a pre-window connectivity test T-48h.

Appendix: short checklist for CS to customize email
- Insert customer-facing name and primary contact
- Note any special exceptions (pinned models, custom connectors)
- Confirm local timezone display in subject and first line

End of document
